articles.title: I rebuilt my portfolio as a chat window with live visitors
articles.summary:
My new site, https://patrickofilada.dev, is one page that behaves like an AI chat. It "thinks" through a few steps, streams in a short intro, and answers "show me your work" with my work history.

The idea comes from Eduardo Alba's site (https://eduardoalba.com). I liked it so much that I built my own version.

Next.js on AWS Amplify. The work history loads only when someone asks for it, so the first page stays light.

articles.title: Open-source chat assistant - cross-platform reply drafter
articles.summary:
TL;DR: jev-chat sits on top of your messaging apps by leveraging accessibility services on Android, on-device OCR on desktop, and custom keyboards on iOS to intercept and read chat windows. Best for: Developers and power users seeking an open-source assistant to manage heavy chat loads across multiple devices.

articles.title: Kotlin Data Class vs Regular Class Explained Simply
articles.summary:
In short: a data class is a normal class where the compiler writes five things for you: equals(), hashCode(), toString(), copy() and component1(), component2() and so on. It uses only the properties in the primary constructor, and copy() copies values, not the objects inside them.


You add an item to the cart, the ViewModel updates its StateFlow, and the screen does not change. No crash, nothing in Logcat. The state is a data class and the update uses copy(). The bug is in how copy() and equals() work together.

articles.title: Build vs Buy in 2026: No-Code Stacks That Hold Up Past MVP
articles.summary:
Every indie founder asks the same question: build with no-code or write code? The answer isn't either/or — it's strategic. Some parts of your SaaS should be no-code (saving months of development). Others must be custom code (protecting your competitive advantage). Here's the framework.


  
  
  Quick Verdict


Bubble remains the most capable general-purpose no-code platform for SaaS. FlutterFlow wins for mobile-first apps. Directual is the best backend-as-a-service approach. But the real question isn't which tool — it's which parts of your product should be no-code.

articles.title: Google Open Sources Ambient Quality Agent (AQuA) to Diagnose Production AI Agent Failures
articles.summary: Google has open-sourced AQuA, a reference implementation that analyzes production AI agent sessions, verifies recurring failure patterns, and investigates root causes against deployed source snapshots.
